I think several of the lessons that are out there you have a very strong what I would call kind of hawkish foreign policy establishment both in Washington and within the Congress so people who really feel that we should be in every conflict, that it's really in America's interest to be in every conflict. That's one part of it. I think there's kind of a sense with members of Congress and congressional leaders that they should be tough. on national security issues. And I would tell you there's no doubt that we should be strong on our national security interests and we should do everything we can to make sure that America is protected. But just sometimes pushing the language out there so far you get yourself in a situation where your pushing is to go into some kind of conflict where we shouldn't be in. And so there are a number of lessons I think that are out there that we've learned. But one of the additional lessons I would say is that there's bipartisanship on this issue. I've worked with Senator Rand Paul, Senator Mike Lee on resolutions that have to do with the 9-11 2001 resolution, authorization of force, and then also on Iran that we shouldn't go to a war with Iran until we have the authorization by Congress rather than having the president get us in a situation. I know you're a scholar on these kinds of things. I mean, one of the most interesting things to me on history is that Michael Beschloss has written this book about presidents going to war. And what you realize looking at many of these wars is we slipped into them with mistakes. It wasn't a thoughtful process by Congress deciding whether there was an absolute necessity that we get into a war. And if Congress does that, and then you have the support of Congress and support of the American people, then I think that's why you get into a conflict and why you get into a war. But we tend to slip into these things and many times a president will take us in. without the approval of Congress, without an authorization, and then we're stuck there for many years.
